subproblem.title: Differentiation of radial cutoff integrals in the scale parameter
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ a Borel measure on E that is finite on compact sets, f: E → ℝ, φ: ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, ξ ∈ E and c, R, A, τ ∈ ℝ with φ(t) = 0 for all t ≥ c, c > 0, τ > 0, cτ < R, f a.e. strongly measurable for μ restricted to B_R(ξ), and |f(x)| ≤ A for all x ∈ B_R(ξ). Then x ↦ f(x)φ(|x − ξ|/τ) and x ↦ f(x)·(−(|x − ξ|/τ²)·φ'(|x − ξ|/τ)) are μ-integrable, and t ↦ ∫ f(x)φ(|x − ξ|/t) dμ(x) has derivative ∫ f(x)·(−(|x − ξ|/τ²)·φ'(|x − ξ|/τ)) dμ(x) at t = τ.

1. (Signs.) R > cτ > 0, so ξ ∈ B and A ≥ |f(ξ)| ≥ 0. Since φ is C¹, φ' is continuous; since φ ≡ 0 on the open set (c, ∞), φ'(s) = 0 for all s > c.
2. (A neighbourhood of τ.) Let δ := min(τ/2, (R − cτ)/(2c)) > 0 and N := (τ − δ, τ + δ). For t ∈ N: t > τ − δ ≥ τ/2 > 0, and ct < c(τ + δ) ≤ cτ + (R − cτ)/2 < R.
3. (Vanishing off B.) For t ∈ N and x ∉ B: r > R > ct, so r/t > c, whence φ(r/t) = 0 and φ'(r/t) = 0; thus F(t, x) = F'(t, x) = 0.

5. (Measurability.) For t ∈ N, F(t, ·) = 1_B·F(t, ·) by 3, and on B it is the product of f, which is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable, with the continuous function x ↦ φ(r/t); hence F(t, ·) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff). The same argument applies to F'(t, ·), since x ↦ −(r/t²)φ'(r/t) is continuous.
6. (Integrability.) μ(B) < ∞ because B is compact. By 3–5, |F(τ, ·)| ≤ A·M₀·1_B and |F'(t, ·)| ≤ C₁·1_B for every t ∈ N, and C₁·1_B is μ-integrable; so F(τ, ·) and F'(τ, ·) are μ-integrable — the first two conclusions.
7. (Pointwise derivative.) Fix x and t ∈ N (so t > 0). The map t ↦ r/t has derivative −r/t² at t, and φ is differentiable, so by the chain rule t ↦ φ(r/t) has derivative φ'(r/t)·(−r/t²); multiplying by the constant f(x), t ↦ F(t, x) has derivative F'(t, x) at t.
8. (Dominated differentiation.) subproblem.title: Radial cutoff fields h·γ(|x−ξ|)(x−ξ) are test fields (parent Step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U ⊆ E open, h: E → ℝ with h ∈ C¹(U) (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U), γ: ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, ξ ∈ E and a, b ∈ ℝ with a > 0, γ(t) = γ(0) for every t ≤ a, γ(t) = 0 for every t ≥ b, and tsupport h ∩ B_b(ξ) ⊆ U (B_b(ξ) the closed ball). Then the vector field X(x) := (h(x)·γ(|x − ξ|))·(x − ξ) is a test field in U (IsTestField U X): X is C¹ on all of E, X has compact support, and tsupport X ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (a b : ℝ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → 0 < a → (∀ t, t ≤ a → γ t = γ 0) → (∀ t, b ≤ t → γ t = 0) → tsupport h ∩ closedBall ξ b ⊆ U → IsTestField U (fun x ↦ (h x * γ ‖x - ξ‖) • (x - ξ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball; r = r(x) := |x − ξ|; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; φ' := deriv φ. This is Step 2 of the parent proof, for an arbitrary profile γ (the parent uses γ(t) = φ(t/τ), a = τ, b = (1+ε)τ).
1. (The set K.) Put K := tsupport h ∩ B_b(ξ). K is closed (intersection of the closed sets tsupport h and B_b(ξ)) and contained in the closed ball B_b(ξ), which is compact because E is finite-dimensional; hence K is compact (IsCompact.inter_left). By hypothesis K ⊆ U.
2. (X vanishes off K.) Let x ∉ K. If x ∉ tsupport h, then h(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so X(x) = 0. If x ∈ tsupport h, then x ∉ B_b(ξ), i.e. |x − ξ| > b; since γ vanishes on [b, ∞), γ(|x − ξ|) = 0 and X(x) = 0.

Write r = |x − ξ|, q_ξ = V.normalRadialSq ξ, ∇^M h = V.tangentialGradient h. Assume (RFV): for every C¹ function γ: ℝ → ℝ such that x ↦ (h(x)γ(r))(x − ξ) is a test field in U, ∫_U [h(nγ(r) + r·γ'(r)·(1 − q_ξ)) + γ(r)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h⟩] dμ = −∫_U h·γ(r)·⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ. Then there exist real numbers R and A with ρ < R such that: h and q_ξ are a.e. strongly measurable for μ restricted to B_R(ξ); |h(x)| ≤ A and |q_ξ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ B_R(ξ); G(x) := ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩ is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ); and for every ε > 0 with (1 + ε)ρ < R, every C¹ function φ: ℝ → ℝ with φ(t) = 1 for t ≤ 1 and φ(t) = 0 for t ≥ 1 + ε, and every τ with 0 < τ ≤ ρ, n·∫ h φ(r/τ) dμ + ∫ h(1 − q_ξ)·((r/τ)φ'(r/τ)) dμ + ∫ φ(r/τ)·G dμ = 0 (integrals over E).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball; r = r(x) := |x − ξ|; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; φ' := deriv φ. μ := V.weight, p_x := (T_xV).starProjection, ∇h := gradient h, ∇^M h(x) = p_x(∇h(x)), q := q_ξ. This child carries out Steps 0, 1 and the first half of Step 3 of the parent proof; the first-variation identity of the sibling theorem radial_first_variation is supplied as the hypothesis (RFV).
1. (Room; parent Step 0.) W := (E ∖ tsupport h) ∪ U is open, and B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ W (a point of B_ρ(ξ) lying in tsupport h lies in U by hypothesis). B_ρ(ξ) is compact, so there is δ > 0 such that the closed δ-neighbourhood of B_ρ(ξ), which equals B_{ρ+δ}(ξ) (cthickening_closedBall), is contained in W (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). [Equivalently, as in the parent proof: otherwise there are x_m ∈ tsupport h ∩ B_{ρ+1/m}(ξ) ∖ U, a subsequence converges to some x ∈ tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) with x ∉ U (tsupport h and E ∖ U are closed), contradicting tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U.] Put R := ρ + δ > ρ and B := B_R(ξ). Then K := tsupport h ∩ B ⊆ U, K is compact, and every x ∈ B ∖ U lies outside tsupport h.
2. (h and ∇h on B.) h is continuous at every x ∈ B: if x ∈ U because h ∈ C¹(U) and U is open; if x ∉ U then x ∉ tsupport h and h ≡ 0 on the open neighbourhood E ∖ tsupport h of x. Likewise ∇h is continuous at every x ∈ B: on the open set U, Dh is continuous (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen) and ∇h is Dh composed with the inverse Riesz isomorphism (InnerProductSpace.toDual); if x ∉ tsupport h then Dh(y) = 0 for all y near x (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport), so ∇h ≡ 0 near x. In particular h(x) = 0 and ∇h(x) = 0 for every x ∉ tsupport h. As B is compact there are A, A₁ ≥ 0 with |h| ≤ A and |∇h| ≤ A₁ on B (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn); h and ∇h are continuous on the closed set B, hence a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable).
3. (∇^M h.) By (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, hence μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable; since the evaluation map (L, v) ↦ Lv is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply), ∇^M h(x) = p_x(∇h(x)) is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). |∇^M h(x)| ≤ |∇h(x)| ≤ A₁ on B because orthogonal projections do not increase norms (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le), and ∇^M h(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport h.
4. (q.) The orthogonal projection onto (T_xV)^⊥ is 1 − p_x (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal'), so q(x) = |(x − ξ) − p_x(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|². Hence q is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (p_x(x − ξ) is, by (FV3) and continuity of evaluation; then differences, norms, squares and the quotient of a.e.-measurable real functions are a.e. measurable), and so is its restriction to B. Moreover 0 ≤ q ≤ 1 everywhere: |p^⊥v| ≤ |v|, and for x = ξ the quotient is 0/0 = 0. In particular |q(x)| ≤ 1 on B.
5. (H on K.) H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) (first conjunct of HasMeanCurvatureIn) and K ⊆ U is compact, so H is μ-integrable on K (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset). Consequently, if c: E → ℝ is μ⌞K-a.e. strongly measurable and |c| ≤ C on K, then x ↦ h(x)c(x)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ is μ-integrable on K: it is μ⌞K-a.e. strongly measurable and bounded on K by A·|C|·R·|H(x)|, which is integrable on K.
6. (G integrable on B.) By bilinearity, G(x) = ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩ + h(x)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩. The first term is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable and bounded on B by R·A₁, and μ(B) < ∞ (B compact, μ finite on compacts), so it is integrable on B. The second term coincides on B with 1_K·h⟨x − ξ, H⟩ (on B ∖ K, x ∉ tsupport h so h(x) = 0), which is integrable by 5 with c ≡ 1. Hence G is μ-integrable on B. Steps 1–6 give ρ < R and the measurability, boundedness and integrability conjuncts.
7. (The test field; parent Step 2.) Fix ε > 0 with (1 + ε)ρ < R, φ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞), and τ ∈ (0, ρ]. φ' is continuous and φ'(t) = 0 for t > 1 + ε (φ ≡ 0 on the open set (1 + ε, ∞)). Since (1 + ε)τ ≤ (1 + ε)ρ < R, we have K_τ := tsupport h ∩ B_{(1+ε)τ}(ξ) ⊆ K ⊆ U. Put γ(t) := φ(t/τ); γ is C¹, γ(t) = 1 = γ(0) for t ≤ τ, γ(t) = 0 for t ≥ (1 + ε)τ. By the sibling lemma weighted_mono_radial_test_field (with a := τ, b := (1 + ε)τ), x ↦ (h(x)γ(r))(x − ξ) is a test field in U, so (RFV) holds for this γ. By the chain rule γ'(t) = φ'(t/τ)/τ, hence r·γ'(r) = (r/τ)φ'(r/τ).
8. (From U to E.) Let x ∉ U; then x ∉ K_τ, so either x ∉ tsupport h, in which case h(x) = 0 and ∇^M h(x) = 0, or r > (1 + ε)τ, in which case r/τ > 1 + ε and φ(r/τ) = φ'(r/τ) = 0. Put T₁ := hφ(r/τ), T₂ := h(1 − q)·((r/τ)φ'(r/τ)), T₃ := φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h⟩, Q := hφ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, H⟩. For x ∉ B we have r > R > (1 + ε)τ, so φ(r/τ) = φ'(r/τ) = 0 and T₁ = T₂ = T₃ = 0 there. On B they are μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable (steps 2–4; r is continuous) and bounded by A·M₀, A·(R/τ)·M₁ (using |1 − q| ≤ 1) and M₀·R·A₁ respectively; since μ(B) < ∞ they are μ-integrable. Q = 1_K·hφ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, H⟩ (off K either h(x) = 0 or x ∉ B and then φ(r/τ) = 0), which is μ-integrable by 5 with c := φ(r/τ), C := M₀.
10. (Assembling; parent Step 3.) By 7, the left (RFV) integrand equals n·T₁ + T₂ + T₃ pointwise (expand h(nφ(r/τ) + (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − q)) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h⟩), and the right integrand is Q. subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball; r = r(x) := |x − ξ|; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; φ' := deriv φ. This is Steps 5–6 of the parent proof together with the integrability statements of its Step 1. Put B := B_R(ξ).
0. (Preliminaries.) ρ, R > 0, ξ ∈ B, A ≥ 0, μ(B) < ∞. u is μ-integrable on B (μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by A on a set of finite measure).
1. (A cutoff family.) Let ψ := Real.smoothTransition: ψ is C^∞, nondecreasing, ψ = 0 on (−∞, 0], ψ = 1 on [1, ∞) and 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1. For ε > 0 put φ_ε(t) := 1 − ψ((t − 1)/ε). Then φ_ε is C¹, nonincreasing, φ_ε(t) = 1 for t ≤ 1, φ_ε(t) = 0 for t ≥ 1 + ε, and 0 ≤ φ_ε ≤ 1 (this is SimonGMT's monotonicityCutoff).
2. (Widths.) ε₁ := min(1, (R/ρ − 1)/2) > 0; then ε₁ ≤ 1 and (1 + ε₁)ρ ≤ (ρ + R)/2 < R. Put ε_m := ε₁/(m + 1) for m ∈ ℕ: 0 < ε_m ≤ ε₁ ≤ 1, (1 + ε_m)ρ < R and ε_m → 0. Write φ_m := φ_{ε_m}, k_m := k_{φ_m}. By hypothesis (S_{φ_m}) holds for every m.
3. (Pointwise limit of cutoffs.) If t ≤ 1, φ_m(t) = 1 for all m. If t > 1, then ε_m < t − 1 for m large, so φ_m(t) = 0 eventually. Hence φ_m(t) → 1 if t ≤ 1 and → 0 if t > 1.
4. (Vanishing off B.) If 0 < t ≤ ρ and x ∉ B, then r > R > (1 + ε_m)ρ ≥ (1 + ε_m)t, so r/t ≥ 1 + ε_m and φ_m(r/t) = 0.
5. (Cutoff integrals.) Let f be μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable and μ-integrable on B, and 0 < t ≤ ρ. Then ∫φ_m(r/t)f dμ → ∫_{B_t(ξ)}f dμ. Indeed, by dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence): φ_m(r/t)f = 1_B·φ_m(r/t)f (step 4) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |φ_m(r/t)f| ≤ 1_B|f| ∈ L¹(μ) (0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1); and by 3, φ_m(r/t)f(x) → f(x) if r/t ≤ 1, i.e. x ∈ B_t(ξ), and → 0 otherwise, i.e. to 1_{B_t(ξ)}f(x); finally ∫1_{B_t(ξ)}f dμ = ∫_{B_t(ξ)}f dμ. Applying this to f = u with t = ρ and t = σ shows that the left side of (S_{φ_m}) tends to (∫_{B_ρ}u dμ)/ρⁿ − (∫_{B_σ}u dμ)/σⁿ; applying it to f = G and t = τ ∈ (σ, ρ] shows L_m(τ) := ∫φ_m(r/τ)G dμ → L(τ) := ∫_{B_τ(ξ)}G dμ.
6. (The kernel.) Let D_m(s) := φ_m(s/ρ) − φ_m(s/σ). By the sibling lemma weighted_mono_kernel_bounds (applied to φ_m, ε_m), for s > 0: D_m(s)/sⁿ ≤ k_m(s) ≤ (1 + ε_m)ⁿD_m(s)/sⁿ. Consequences: (a) k_m(0) = 0, as the integrand vanishes for s = 0. (b) For s > 0, 0 ≤ D_m(s) ≤ 1, because s/σ ≥ s/ρ, φ_m is nonincreasing and takes values in [0, 1]. (c) D_m(s) = 0 if 0 < s ≤ σ (both arguments are ≤ 1) and if s > (1 + ε_m)ρ (both arguments are ≥ 1 + ε_m); in these cases the squeeze gives k_m(s) = 0. (d) |k_m(s)| ≤ 2ⁿ/σⁿ for all s ≥ 0: trivial in the cases of (a), (c); for s > σ, 0 ≤ k_m(s) ≤ (1 + ε_m)ⁿ·1/sⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ/σⁿ. (e) k_m(r(x)) = 0 for x ∉ B (then r > R > (1 + ε_m)ρ). (f) k_m is Borel measurable: (s, τ) ↦ −(s/τ²)φ_m'(s/τ)/τⁿ is Borel on ℝ², and integrating a jointly measurable function in τ against the σ-finite measure λ⌞(σ,ρ] gives a measurable function of s (StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right). (g) k_m(s) → s^{-n}·1_{σ<s≤ρ} for every s ≥ 0: for s = 0 by (a) (the limit is 0 since σ > 0); for s > 0, D_m(s) → 1_{s≤ρ} − 1_{s≤σ} = 1_{σ<s≤ρ} by 3 (s/ρ ≤ 1 ⟺ s ≤ ρ, s/σ ≤ 1 ⟺ s ≤ σ, σ ≤ ρ), (1 + ε_m)ⁿ → 1, so both bounds converge to s^{-n}1_{σ<s≤ρ} and so does k_m(s) (squeeze).
7. (Kernel integral.) ∫u·q·k_m(r)dμ → ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ}u·(q/rⁿ)dμ by dominated convergence: u q k_m(r) = 1_B·u q k_m(r) (6(e)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (6(f)); |u q k_m(r)| ≤ A·2ⁿσ^{-n}·1_B, integrable (6(d)); and by 6(g) it converges pointwise to u q r^{-n}1_{σ<r≤ρ} = 1_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)}·u·(q/rⁿ) (x ∈ B_ρ ∖ B_σ ⟺ σ < r ≤ ρ).
8. (Curvature term.) For τ ∈ (σ, ρ], |L_m(τ)| ≤ C_G := ∫_B|G|dμ (|φ_m(r/τ)G| ≤ 1_B|G|). L_m is continuous on [σ, ρ] (dominated continuity of parameter integrals: the integrand is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, dominated by 1_B|G|, continuous in τ > 0), so τ ↦ L_m(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ is a.e. strongly measurable on (σ, ρ] and bounded there by C_G/σⁿ⁺¹; by 5 it converges pointwise on (σ, ρ] to L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹. Since λ((σ, ρ]) < ∞, dominated convergence gives ∫_{(σ,ρ]}L_m(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹dτ → ∫_{(σ,ρ]}L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹dτ.
9. (The identity (iii).) By 5, 7 and 8 the two sides of (S_{φ_m}) converge to the two sides of (iii); since they are equal for every m, the limits coincide (uniqueness of limits in ℝ).
10. (Integrability (i).) τ ↦ L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ is the pointwise a.e. limit on (σ, ρ] of the a.e. strongly measurable functions L_m(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ (step 8), so it is a.e. strongly measurable for λ⌞(σ,ρ] (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae), and its absolute value is ≤ C_G/σⁿ⁺¹ (limit of the uniform bounds). A bounded a.e.-measurable function on a set of finite Lebesgue measure is integrable. [Alternatively, as in the parent proof, L(τ) = ∫_{B_τ}(1_B G)⁺dμ − ∫_{B_τ}(1_B G)⁻dμ for τ ≤ ρ is a difference of two nondecreasing functions of τ, hence Borel.]
11. (Integrability (ii).) On the annulus B_ρ(ξ) ∖ B_σ(ξ) ⊆ B we have r > σ, |u| ≤ A and |q| ≤ 1, so |u·q/rⁿ| ≤ A/σⁿ; the function is a.e. strongly measurable for μ restricted to the annulus (u, q are, and r is continuous), and the annulus has finite μ-measure (≤ μ(B)). Hence it is μ-integrable on the annulus.

Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball; r = r(x) := |x − ξ|; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; φ' := deriv φ. This is Steps 3 (second half) and 4 of the parent proof for one cutoff φ. 0. (Preliminaries.) R > (1 + ε)ρ > 0, ξ ∈ B, A ≥ 0, μ(B) < ∞. For τ ∈ [σ, ρ]: τ ≥ σ > 0 and (1 + ε)τ ≤ (1 + ε)ρ < R. uq is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable with |uq| ≤ A on B. φ'(t) = 0 for t > 1 + ε. For τ ∈ [σ, ρ] and x ∉ B, r > R > (1 + ε)τ, so φ(r/τ) = φ'(r/τ) = 0; for x ∈ B, r/τ ∈ [0, R/σ]. Let M₀, M₁ be the maxima of |φ|, |φ'| on [0, R/σ].

Likewise L is continuous on [σ, ρ]: the integrand φ(r/τ)G(x) equals 1_B·φ(r/τ)G(x) (step 0), is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (G is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable, being integrable on B), is dominated by M₀|G|1_B ∈ L¹(μ), and is continuous in τ. Since τ ≥ σ > 0 on [σ, ρ], F' is continuous there.
5. (Fundamental theorem of calculus.) By 3, F has derivative F'(τ) at every τ ∈ [σ, ρ], and F' is continuous, hence interval integrable, on [σ, ρ] (step 4). So F(ρ) − F(σ) = ∫_σ^ρ F'(τ)dτ = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} J₁(τ)/τⁿdτ + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹dτ (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le; both summands are continuous on [σ, ρ] and hence integrable on (σ, ρ]).
